question.text: The atomic mass of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><none></none><mn>12</mn><mprescripts></mprescripts><mn>6</mn><none></none></mmultiscripts></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>12</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>000000</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi></math> and that of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><none></none><mn>13</mn><mprescripts></mprescripts><mn>6</mn><none></none></mmultiscripts></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>13</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>003354</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi></math>. The required energy to remove a neutron from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><none></none><mn>13</mn><mprescripts></mprescripts><mn>6</mn><none></none></mmultiscripts></math>, if mass of neutron is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>008665</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi></math>, will be:

solution.text:
Given the nuclear reaction is

C136+Energy→C126+n10

The mass defect for the above reaction can be calculated as follows:

Δm=(12.000000+1.008665)-13.003354 u=-0.00531 u

Hence, the energy required is given by

E=0.00531×931.5 MeV=4.95 MeV
